title: Interlude: Three Men and a Letter
summary: Marchand's POV, Founding Night, the Halyard bar. Marchand composes the denunciation item by item: the Fulvian footwork in the sand, a Collar who stands like a plate-bearer, an unreported salvage from a founding-era hull, and a sealed packet addressed to a senator named Vibius, taken from Ochoa's effects. He does not write what he saw in the hold. Corin, on the rolls and terrified of what he watched, signs as witness. Gaspar, drunk, says 'Tom's boy' and nothing else. Marchand posts the letter through the quaestor's slot at the sixth bell. His unwritten third reason: the boy stood over a dead Stripe and was not sorry.

events.description: Marchand inventoried Ochoa's locker on the second day and found it clean; the unmanifested packets Ochoa carried for six years were gone. He heard the name 'Vibius' in the hold.
Corin admits he would have lost to the cadet and that Jonah's step cannot have been learned on Anvil; he wanted Jonah 'not here' before he ships out.
Marchand writes the denunciation: unlawful lorica or object from a founding-era hull, and a sealed packet for a senator named Vibius, correspondence of an unlawful faction. He omits Varro's death.
Corin signs as witness with an unsteady hand. Gaspar wakes, says 'Tom's boy. He's a good boy', and goes back to sleep.
Marchand posts the letter through the petition slot of the quaestor's house at the sixth bell, marked urgent and concerning the Flamens.

thread_beats.description: The letter written, signed, witnessed by silence, and posted. The reader knows the four names' first three and their reasons.
Marchand for the captaincy and fear; Corin for Mara and for the bout he could not have won; Gaspar for nothing, which is his crime.
Marchand names Vibius in writing. The seal is now sedition on paper, addressed to the quaestor whose father it names.
Corin's confession: 'she'll be watching him do things I can't.' He signs.

clues.description: Marchand does not write the hold. He writes only the sand and the packet.
clues.mechanism: Why Priscus can dismiss the lorica (ch.6) and bury on the seal instead; why Varro's death stays a Vigilant mystery until ch.34.

clues.description: Ochoa carried small sealed things unmanifested for six years, aboard on Anvil, off in the Interior.

clues.description: Corin's hand signing is the hand of a man in the sand who has decided and is about to be cut.
clues.mechanism: Corin falls on a duelling floor in Book 3.

clues.description: Gaspar decided long ago that the safest thing a Collar can do in any room is nothing.
clues.mechanism: Ch.35: he sells the story to a stranger because a stranger is not a room.

opening_hook: Marchand had never written a number he had not checked, and he was not going to start with a letter.
closing_hook: A boy with a ring on his finger lies awake and does not know he has six days.
